questions.stem: Three vans each carry at most 1,000 kg. To save variables, a planner drops the van index and writes one row: the total weight shipped is at most 3,000 kg. What does that model's optimum tell the planner?

options.text: The value the three vans can carry, since the totals are equal
options.says: Equal totals are not equal models: on the OR-Tools example the pooled row promised 410 where five bins allow 395.

options.text: A lower bound on that value, since one row allows fewer loads
options.says: Adding the van rows up gives the pooled row, so every loading the vans allow obeys it: the pooled row allows more loads, not fewer.

options.text: Nothing, since the one row may refuse loads the vans allow
options.says: Every packing into the vans obeys the pooled row; it refuses none of them.

options.text: An upper bound on that value, perhaps above every real loading
options.says: Right: the pooled model is a relaxation, so its optimum bounds the vans' value from above and may not be reachable.

origin.section: Several Knapsacks Share the Items: One Binary per Item and Knapsack

questions.stem: Every inspection i must be done by one of four inspectors; inspector k needs h[i,k] hours for it and has H[k] hours. Which rows state this, with x[i,k] binary?

options.text: Per inspection, x[i,k] summed over k is at most 1; per inspector, h[i,k] x[i,k] summed over i is at most H[k]
options.says: 'At most 1' lets an inspection go to no one; the rule says each must be done, so the row is an equality.

options.text: Per inspection, x[i,k] summed over k equals 1; per inspector, h[i,k] x[i,k] summed over i is at most H[k]
options.says: Right: equality assignment rows and one capacity row per agent with that agent's sizes, the GAP of the lesson.

options.text: Per inspection, x[i,k] summed over k equals 1; per inspector, x[i,k] summed over i is at most H[k]
options.says: That row counts inspections, not hours: each agent's capacity row charges a task its size for that agent, h[i,k].

options.text: Per inspection, x[i,k] summed over k is at least 1; per inspector, h[i,k] x[i,k] summed over i is at most H[k]
options.says: 'At least 1' lets two inspectors share one inspection; each task goes to exactly one agent, so the row is an equality.

origin.section: Every Item Goes to Exactly One Agent, at a Size That Depends on the Agent

questions.stem: In a job-to-crew assignment, a job in a district may only go to crews holding that district's permit. How is that rule best put into the model?

options.text: A row x[i,k] = 0 for every job and every crew in the model
options.says: That forbids every assignment, permitted or not; only the forbidden pairs may be held at 0.

options.text: A capacity of 0 for each crew that lacks some district's permit
options.says: The rule removes pairs, not crews: Coast and Plains kept their capacity and did the work they are allowed to do.

options.text: No variable x[i,k] at all for a job-crew pair the rule forbids
options.says: Right: like a timing window, a forbidden pair simply has no variable, so no row can assign it.

options.text: One variable per job, with its crew picked after the solve
options.says: One binary per job cannot say which crew does it, so the capacity rows could not be written.

origin.section: An Agent That May Not Take an Item Gets No Variable
